headline: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50 percent, its first hike since February 2023, hours before Federal Reserve minutes showed officials still expecting to tighten further, so the two central banks are now pointing the same way with Brent above 100 dollars and the dollar index at the top of its 52 week range.

summary.us: The S&P 500 slipped 0.22 percent to 7,801.77 and the Nasdaq Composite fell the same 0.22 percent to 27,538.69, both a day after records, while the Dow lost 0.66 percent to 51,179.87 as the 10 year Treasury yield touched its highest level since 2002 before a solid 10 year auction pulled it back to 5.277 percent. Minutes of the 15 and 16 September meeting showed officials expecting further rate increases without saying when, and October hike pricing sits near 22 percent against roughly 51 percent a week earlier.
summary.india: The Monetary Policy Committee raised the repo rate to 5.50 percent and shifted its stance to calibrated tightening, citing broadening inflation and Brent above 100 dollars, and the Nifty 50 closed 0.76 percent lower at 22,603.05 while the Bank Nifty held up better at 55,055.55, down 0.13 percent. Provisional exchange data put foreign institutional investors at about 6,121 crore rupees of net cash selling against roughly 4,597 crore rupees of domestic buying, and the rupee weakened to 96.658 per dollar, within a whisker of its 52 week low.
summary.global: The Nikkei 225 gave back 0.95 percent and the Hang Seng fell 0.62 percent to 24,130.50 with mainland China shut for Golden Week, while a gilt selloff that pushed 30 year UK yields above 6 percent left the FTSE 100 down 0.79 percent and HSBC down 4.36 percent in London. Copper rose 2.05 percent to sit just under its 52 week high even as gold fell 0.84 percent to 4,151.90 dollars and silver 0.98 percent, and iron ore names such as Rio Tinto dropped on Chinese demand worries while Brent held near 101 dollars against WTI at 89.37.

calendar.what: TCS board meets on Q2 FY27 results and a possible second interim dividend, earnings call in the evening IST. Record date for the dividend is set for 14 October
TSMC September monthly revenue, 13:30 Taipei time. August revenue was about 514.8 billion New Taiwan dollars, up 53.3 percent year on year
US weekly initial jobless claims, 8:30 am ET. PepsiCo opens the US third quarter reporting season
Preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment, 10:00 am ET, forecast 47.6 against 47.8 previously
India Q2 results: Poonawalla Fincorp, Can Fin Homes and Anand Rathi Wealth
HCL Technologies Q2 FY27 results. Columbus Day in the US, no major data release. Reliance Jio is reported to be filing final offer documents with SEBI this week

US bank earnings: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan around 7:00 am ET with the call at 8:30 am ET. Consensus for JPMorgan is about 5.90 dollars a share on 51.19 billion dollars of revenue
HD Fire Protect IPO opens on the Indian mainboard. Reserve Bank of Australia policy meeting
US September CPI, 8:30 am ET. The latest year on year reading was 3.4 percent. China CPI the same day, and Bank of America Q3 results
US September PPI and advance retail sales, both 8:30 am ET. Wipro and Tech Mahindra Q2 results. Tesla Roadster reveal, moved from 1 October

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.
